valuation.method: Forward EPS x justified P/E: FY2027 diluted adjusted EPS viewed at the 12-month target date (Nov 2027), times a justified P/E. USD listing, no ADR conversion, price-only (dividends excluded). Anchors: FY2025 adjusted EPS $12.20 (Feb 11 2026 release); FY2026 operating margin guided to the mid-to-high 40% range with a $0.20-0.30 FX tailwind; Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $3.57 (+11% constant currency) reported Nov 4 2026. FY2026 EPS of about $13.10 (7-8% growth) and FY2027 EPS are my own assumptions; the 9M 2026 quarterly EPS and the FY2026 guidance table were not read directly.

bear.driver: Low-single-digit U.S. traffic keeps comps weak, 2027 food and paper inflation in the mid-single digits is not fully passed through, and the value-program investment dilutes margin; the stock stays de-rated.

base.driver: Global comps grow mid-single digits with franchising mix and cost efficiencies (systems and data benefits from 2027) lifting EPS about 7%; the multiple stays near a modest discount to its recent level.

bull.driver: U.S. comps turn clearly positive on the value platform and check growth, margins rise further from refranchising, and buybacks add to EPS growth; the premium defensive multiple returns.

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS of $14.00 the $271.97 close implies 19.4x. The aggregate Street mean target of $299 implies 21.4x on the same EPS, and the two dated named targets (Tigress $390, Guggenheim $250) average $320 and imply 22.9x.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $14.00 (about 5.1 pp of the close); a $0.50 change in FY2027 EPS at 21.5x moves it by about $10.75 (3.9 pp).
valuation.watch_metric: U.S. comparable sales (Q3 2026: down 0.2%, positive in September) with guest counts, and global operating margin in the mid-to-high 40s, together with 2027 EPS guidance that reflects the 2027 food and paper inflation and the value-program cost.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 and FY2026 results with 2027 outlook, expected in early February 2027 (date not confirmed in sources).

analyst_notes: Only two named analysts have dated calls I could verify through the cutoff: Ivan Feinseth at Tigress (Buy, $390 from $385 on Jul 17) and Gregory Francfort at Guggenheim (Neutral, $250 from $290 on Oct 5, cutting after Analyst Day). Their equal-weight target is $320 and the 90-day weighted target about $299 (raw weights 0.40 and 0.74, normalized about 35% and 65%), but neither has a documented 12-month horizon, so both stay out of the weighted target. Firm-only dated actions (KeyCorp Overweight $305 to $280 on Oct 6; HSBC Buy $357 to $356 on Aug 5; DZ Bank Buy reissued Sep 24) lack a named analyst and are excluded from the individual calculation; the undated post-Q3 moves (Wells Fargo Overweight $270 to $300, BTIG Buy $295 to $305, RBC $285 to $300, Bernstein Market Perform $250 to $280, Freedom Broker Hold $305 to $298) are excluded because their dates are not verified. The aggregate Street mean of $299 (29 analysts, Yahoo Finance via yfinance) runs about 10% above the close and about 1 pp below my base case, so the gap is small and within rounding of the EPS assumption.
